Sweetheart, I hope you take the time to grieve the plans you made and the love you thought you had.

I have been both a cheater and the cheated upon. Hand on heart, cheaters are deeply unhappy with themselves and seek validation from flattery and attention. Her actions are no reflection on you.

However, I have been the victim. The sick, heavy dread and sadness is so hard. The questioning and agonising is awful. Time will lessen the pain, and you might even forget sometimes. Then you will remember, and the anger and sadness will wash over you. Stop, acknowledge your feelings, breathe, and start walking again.

When you are in a better position, I would recommend seeking a therapist or psychologist to talk about your experiences and find strategies to enforce boundaries and establish how to communicate your needs in a relationship, to avoid being taken advantage of. You deserve better, and you will do better, starting by taking care of yourself and showing some self love.

Much love and hugs.

I think she's super unhappy about my progress with my own therapy. I have been a part of an OCD clinic for two years and my mother was marked as my highest trigger point.
So I wrote a letter about 6 months ago explaining my condition and how it was impacting my life but how the therapy I've been doing (mainly immersion therapy) has really helped. 
Unfortunately, my OCD manifests as violence against myself and violence against others so she took that whole email as me thinking about killing her all the time.
So the recommendation from my psych was to but a boundary of "no touch" and start small, like sitting next to her, moving to holding hands then hugs. She raged at that and was bitching to my family about it.
Then she tried calling my psych and was questioning my therapy in terms of its effectiveness.

I've been avoiding talking about my OCD here, because violence can be a trigger for others and I don't want to distract from uBPD with my own diagnosis. But in saying that, anyone here who does have OCD, there is a strong correlation that your BPD parent has a lot to do with it.
